1	"""Self-describing columnar file format.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	* :class:`ColumnSchema` / :class:`Schema` / :class:`Table` -- in-memory model
6	* :func:`write_file` -- deterministic, atomic write
7	* :func:`read_file` -- strict, validating read with optional projection
8	* :func:`inspect_file` -- metadata-only read
9	* :class:`ColumnarFormatError` -- raised for every malformed-file condition
10	
11	File layout (little-endian)::
12	
13	    b"CAEF"            magic
14	    uint8              format version
15	    uint32             header byte length
16	    <header bytes>     UTF-8 JSON, schema + per-column stats/chunk pointers
17	    <data section>     raw concatenated column payloads, or zlib of the same
18	    uint32             CRC-32 of every preceding byte
19	    b"END1"            end marker
20	
21	The same schema, values and options always produce identical bytes: the JSON
22	header uses a fixed key order and compact separators, there are no timestamps,
23	and zlib is invoked with a fixed level.
24	"""
25	
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import json
29	import os
30	import struct
31	import tempfile
32	import zlib
33	from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
34	from dataclasses import dataclass
35	from typing import Any
36	
37	__all__ = [
38	    "FORMAT_VERSION",
39	    "ColumnarFormatError",
40	    "ColumnSchema",
41	    "Schema",
42	    "Table",
43	    "write_file",
44	    "read_file",
45	    "inspect_file",
46	]
47	
48	FORMAT_VERSION = 1
49	
50	_MAGIC = b"CAEF"
51	_FOOTER_MARKER = b"END1"
52	_TYPE_NAMES = ("bool", "int64", "float64", "utf8")
53	_ENCODING_NAMES = ("plain", "dictionary")
54	_COMPRESSION_NAMES = ("none", "zlib")
55	_HEADER_KEYS = frozenset(
56	    ("compression", "row_count", "data_length", "data_crc32", "uncompressed_length", "columns")
57	)
58	_COLUMN_KEYS = frozenset(
59	    ("name", "type", "nullable", "encoding", "offset", "length", "crc32",
60	     "null_count", "min", "max")
61	)
62	_PREFIX_LEN = 9  # magic(4) + version(1) + header length uint32
63	_FOOTER_LEN = 8  # crc32 uint32 + marker
64	_MAX_HEADER_BYTES = 256 * 1024 * 1024
65	
66	
67	class ColumnarFormatError(Exception):
68	    """Raised when a columnar file is structurally invalid or unsupported."""
69	
70	
71	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
72	# In-memory model
73	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
74	
75	
76	@dataclass(frozen=True)
77	class ColumnSchema:
78	    """One column: a non-empty unique Unicode ``name``, a type and nullability."""
79	
80	    name: str
81	    type: str
82	    nullable: bool = False
83	
84	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
85	        if not isinstance(self.name, str) or not self.name:
86	            raise ValueError("column name must be a non-empty string")
87	        try:
88	            self.name.encode("utf-8")
89	        except UnicodeEncodeError:
90	            raise ValueError("column name must contain valid Unicode scalars") from None
91	        if self.type not in _TYPE_NAMES:
92	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported column type: {self.type!r}")
93	        if not isinstance(self.nullable, bool):
94	            raise ValueError("nullable must be a bool")
95	
96	
97	@dataclass(frozen=True)
98	class Schema:
99	    """An ordered, non-empty collection of :class:`ColumnSchema`."""
100	
101	    columns: tuple[ColumnSchema, ...]
102	
103	    def __init__(self, columns: Sequence[ColumnSchema]):
104	        cols = tuple(columns)
105	        if not cols:
106	            raise ValueError("schema must contain at least one column")
107	        for col in cols:
108	            if not isinstance(col, ColumnSchema):
109	                raise ValueError("schema entries must be ColumnSchema instances")
110	        seen: set[str] = set()
111	        for col in cols:
112	            if col.name in seen:
113	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate column name: {col.name!r}")
114	            seen.add(col.name)
115	        object.__setattr__(self, "columns", cols)
116	
117	    @property
118	    def names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
119	        return tuple(col.name for col in self.columns)
120	
121	    def index(self, name: str) -> int:
122	        for i, col in enumerate(self.columns):
123	            if col.name == name:
124	                return i
125	        raise KeyError(name)
126	
127	
128	class Table:
129	    """A schema together with equal-length, column-oriented Python lists."""
130	
131	    def __init__(self, schema: Schema, columns: Mapping[str, Sequence] | Sequence[Sequence]):
132	        if not isinstance(schema, Schema):
133	            raise TypeError("schema must be a Schema instance")
134	        aligned = _align_columns(schema, columns)
135	        row_count = _validate_columns(schema, aligned)
136	        self.schema = schema
137	        self._row_count = row_count
138	        self._columns = tuple(tuple(col) for col in aligned)
139	
140	    @classmethod
141	    def _from_storage(cls, schema: Schema, columns: Sequence[Sequence]) -> "Table":
142	        """Build without re-validating (used by the decoder)."""
143	        obj = cls.__new__(cls)
144	        obj.schema = schema
145	        obj._row_count = len(columns[0]) if columns else 0
146	        obj._columns = tuple(tuple(col) for col in columns)
147	        return obj
148	
149	    @property
150	    def row_count(self) -> int:
151	        return self._row_count
152	
153	    @property
154	    def column_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
155	        return self.schema.names
156	
157	    def column(self, name: str) -> list:
158	        """Return a fresh list of the named column's values."""
159	        return list(self._columns[self.schema.index(name)])
160	
161	    @property
162	    def columns(self) -> dict[str, list]:
163	        """Column name to value list, in schema order."""
164	        return {name: list(self._columns[i]) for i, name in enumerate(self.schema.names)}
165	
166	    def project(self, names: Sequence[str]) -> "Table":
167	        """Return a table restricted to ``names``, in the requested order.
168	
169	        Unknown names raise :class:`KeyError`; repeated names raise
170	        :class:`ValueError`.
171	        """
172	        if isinstance(names, str):
173	            raise ValueError("project names must be a sequence of strings, not a single string")
174	        requested = tuple(names)
175	        if len(set(requested)) != len(requested):
176	            raise ValueError("projection contains duplicate column names")
177	        indices = []
178	        for name in requested:
179	            indices.append(self.schema.index(name))  # KeyError on unknown name
180	        sub_schema = Schema([self.schema.columns[i] for i in indices])
181	        sub_cols = [self._columns[i] for i in indices]
182	        return Table._from_storage(sub_schema, sub_cols)
183	
184	
185	def _align_columns(
186	    schema: Schema, columns: Mapping[str, Sequence] | Sequence[Sequence]
187	) -> list[Sequence]:
188	    if isinstance(columns, Mapping):
189	        missing = [name for name in schema.names if name not in columns]
190	        if missing:
191	            raise ValueError(f"missing column(s): {', '.join(missing)!r}")
192	        extra = [name for name in columns if name not in set(schema.names)]
193	        if extra:
194	            raise ValueError(f"unexpected column(s): {', '.join(map(str, extra))!r}")
195	        return [columns[name] for name in schema.names]
196	    if isinstance(columns, Sequence) and not isinstance(columns, (str, bytes)):
197	        if len(columns) != len(schema.columns):
198	            raise ValueError(
199	                f"expected {len(schema.columns)} columns, got {len(columns)}"
200	            )
201	        return list(columns)
202	    raise TypeError("columns must be a mapping or a sequence aligned to the schema")
203	
204	
205	def _validate_columns(schema: Schema, columns: Sequence[Sequence]) -> int:
206	    """Check shape, nullability, per-value Python types and float finiteness."""
207	    row_count: int | None = None
208	    for col, raw in zip(schema.columns, columns):
209	        try:
210	            values = list(raw)
211	        except TypeError:
212	            raise ValueError(f"column {col.name!r} is not a sequence") from None
213	        if row_count is None:
214	            row_count = len(values)
215	        elif len(values) != row_count:
216	            raise ValueError(
217	                f"column {col.name!r} has {len(values)} rows, expected {row_count}"
218	            )
219	        for position, value in enumerate(values):
220	            where = f"column {col.name!r} row {position}"
221	            if value is None:
222	                if not col.nullable:
223	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: NULL in non-nullable column")
224	                continue
225	            if col.type == "bool":
226	                if not isinstance(value, bool):
227	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: expected bool, got {type(value).__name__}")
228	            elif col.type == "int64":
229	                if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
230	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: expected int64, got {type(value).__name__}")
231	                if not (-(2**63) <= value <= 2**63 - 1):
232	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: value outside int64 range")
233	            elif col.type == "float64":
234	                if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, float):
235	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: expected float64, got {type(value).__name__}")
236	                if value != value or value in (float("inf"), float("-inf")):
237	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: float64 must be finite (no NaN or infinity)")
238	            elif col.type == "utf8":
239	                if not isinstance(value, str):
240	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: expected utf8 string, got {type(value).__name__}")
241	                try:
242	                    value.encode("utf-8")
243	                except UnicodeEncodeError:
244	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: string is not valid UTF-8 Unicode") from None
245	    assert row_count is not None
246	    return row_count
247	
248	
249	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
250	# Encoding
251	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
252	
253	
254	def _pack_bits(flags: Sequence[bool]) -> bytes:
255	    out = bytearray((len(flags) + 7) // 8)
256	    for i, flag in enumerate(flags):
257	        if flag:
258	            out[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)
259	    return bytes(out)
260	
261	
262	def _check_padding(bits: bytes, count: int, what: str) -> None:
263	    if count % 8:
264	        unused = bits[-1] >> (count % 8)
265	        if unused:
266	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"non-zero padding bits in {what}")
267	
268	
269	def _encode_payload(
270	    col: ColumnSchema, values: Sequence, use_dictionary: bool
271	) -> tuple[bytes, int, Any, Any]:
272	    n = len(values)
273	    null_count = 0
274	    minimum: Any = None
275	    maximum: Any = None
276	    validity = bytearray((n + 7) // 8) if col.nullable else None
277	
278	    if col.type == "bool":
279	        flags: list[bool] = []
280	        for i, value in enumerate(values):
281	            if value is None:
282	                flags.append(False)
283	                null_count += 1
284	                continue
285	            if validity is not None:
286	                validity[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)
287	            flags.append(value)
288	            if minimum is None or value < minimum:
289	                minimum = value
290	            if maximum is None or value > maximum:
291	                maximum = value
292	        body = _pack_bits(flags)
293	    elif col.type == "int64":
294	        buf = bytearray()
295	        for i, value in enumerate(values):
296	            if value is None:
297	                buf.extend(b"\x00" * 8)
298	                null_count += 1
299	                continue
300	            if validity is not None:
301	                validity[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)
302	            buf.extend(struct.pack("<q", value))
303	            if minimum is None or value < minimum:
304	                minimum = value
305	            if maximum is None or value > maximum:
306	                maximum = value
307	        body = bytes(buf)
308	    elif col.type == "float64":
309	        buf = bytearray()
310	        for i, value in enumerate(values):
311	            if value is None:
312	                buf.extend(b"\x00" * 8)
313	                null_count += 1
314	                continue
315	            if validity is not None:
316	                validity[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)
317	            buf.extend(struct.pack("<d", value))
318	            if minimum is None or value < minimum:
319	                minimum = value
320	            if maximum is None or value > maximum:
321	                maximum = value
322	        body = bytes(buf)
323	    else:  # utf8
324	        if use_dictionary:
325	            dictionary: list[str] = []
326	            dictionary_index: dict[str, int] = {}
327	            indices = bytearray()
328	            for i, value in enumerate(values):
329	                if value is None:
330	                    indices.extend(struct.pack("<i", -1))
331	                    null_count += 1
332	                    continue
333	                if validity is not None:
334	                    validity[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)
335	                idx = dictionary_index.get(value)
336	                if idx is None:
337	                    # Dictionary ids follow first-occurrence order.
338	                    idx = len(dictionary)
339	                    dictionary_index[value] = idx
340	                    dictionary.append(value)
341	                indices.extend(struct.pack("<i", idx))
342	                if minimum is None or value < minimum:
343	                    minimum = value
344	                if maximum is None or value > maximum:
345	                    maximum = value
346	            body = (
347	                struct.pack("<I", len(dictionary))
348	                + _encode_utf8_strings(dictionary)
349	                + bytes(indices)
350	            )
351	        else:
352	            ordered: list[str] = []
353	            for i, value in enumerate(values):
354	                if value is None:
355	                    ordered.append("")
356	                    null_count += 1
357	                    continue
358	                if validity is not None:
359	                    validity[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)
360	                ordered.append(value)
361	                if minimum is None or value < minimum:
362	                    minimum = value
363	                if maximum is None or value > maximum:
364	                    maximum = value
365	            body = _encode_utf8_strings(ordered)
366	
367	    payload = (bytes(validity) if validity is not None else b"") + body
368	    return payload, null_count, minimum, maximum
369	
370	
371	def _encode_utf8_strings(strings: Sequence[str]) -> bytes:
372	    offsets = bytearray()
373	    blob = bytearray()
374	    cursor = 0
375	    offsets.extend(struct.pack("<I", 0))
376	    for value in strings:
377	        raw = value.encode("utf-8")
378	        cursor += len(raw)
379	        blob.extend(raw)
380	        offsets.extend(struct.pack("<I", cursor))
381	    return bytes(offsets) + bytes(blob)
382	
383	
384	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
385	# Decoding
386	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
387	
388	
389	def _decode_column(
390	    col: ColumnSchema, encoding: str, row_count: int, payload: bytes
391	) -> list:
392	    cursor = 0
393	    validity: bytes | None = None
394	    if col.nullable:
395	        size = (row_count + 7) // 8
396	        if len(payload) < cursor + size:
397	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"truncated validity bitmap for {col.name!r}")
398	        validity = payload[cursor : cursor + size]
399	        _check_padding(validity, row_count, f"validity bitmap of {col.name!r}")
400	        cursor += size
401	    body = payload[cursor:]
402	
403	    if col.type == "bool":
404	        size = (row_count + 7) // 8
405	        if len(body) != size:
406	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"bad bool payload length for {col.name!r}")
407	        _check_padding(body, row_count, f"bool payload of {col.name!r}")
408	        values = [
409	            bool((body[i >> 3] >> (i & 7)) & 1) for i in range(row_count)
410	        ]
411	    elif col.type == "int64":
412	        if len(body) != 8 * row_count:
413	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"bad int64 payload length for {col.name!r}")
414	        values = list(struct.unpack(f"<{row_count}q", body)) if row_count else []
415	    elif col.type == "float64":
416	        if len(body) != 8 * row_count:
417	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"bad float64 payload length for {col.name!r}")
418	        values = list(struct.unpack(f"<{row_count}d", body)) if row_count else []
419	        for i, value in enumerate(values):
420	            if value != value or value in (float("inf"), float("-inf")):
421	                raise ColumnarFormatError(
422	                    f"non-finite float64 stored in {col.name!r} row {i}"
423	                )
424	    elif encoding == "dictionary":
425	        values = _decode_dict_utf8(col, row_count, body, validity)
426	    else:
427	        values = _decode_plain_utf8(col, row_count, body)
428	
429	    if validity is not None:
430	        for i in range(row_count):
431	            if not ((validity[i >> 3] >> (i & 7)) & 1):
432	                values[i] = None
433	    return values
434	
435	
436	def _decode_utf8_blob(col: ColumnSchema, body: bytes, count: int, *, what: str) -> list[str]:
437	    offset_bytes = 4 * (count + 1)
438	    if len(body) < offset_bytes:
439	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"truncated {what} offsets for {col.name!r}")
440	    offsets = struct.unpack(f"<{count + 1}I", body[:offset_bytes])
441	    blob = body[offset_bytes:]
442	    if offsets[0] != 0:
443	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"{what} offsets must start at 0 for {col.name!r}")
444	    for prev, nxt in zip(offsets, offsets[1:]):
445	        if nxt < prev:
446	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"non-monotonic {what} offsets for {col.name!r}")
447	    if offsets[-1] != len(blob):
448	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"{what} byte length mismatch for {col.name!r}")
449	    strings = []
450	    for i in range(count):
451	        raw = blob[offsets[i] : offsets[i + 1]]
452	        try:
453	            strings.append(raw.decode("utf-8"))
454	        except UnicodeDecodeError:
455	            raise ColumnarFormatError(
456	                f"invalid UTF-8 in {what} entry {i} of {col.name!r}"
457	            ) from None
458	    return strings
459	
460	
461	def _decode_plain_utf8(col: ColumnSchema, row_count: int, body: bytes) -> list[str]:
462	    return _decode_utf8_blob(col, body, row_count, what="utf8")
463	
464	
465	def _decode_dict_utf8(
466	    col: ColumnSchema, row_count: int, body: bytes, validity: bytes | None
467	) -> list[str]:
468	    if len(body) < 4:
469	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"truncated dictionary header for {col.name!r}")
470	    (dict_size,) = struct.unpack("<I", body[:4])
471	    rest = body[4:]
472	    offset_bytes = 4 * (dict_size + 1)
473	    # Split dictionary section from the trailing row indices.
474	    if len(rest) < offset_bytes:
475	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"truncated dictionary offsets for {col.name!r}")
476	    tentative_offsets = struct.unpack(f"<{dict_size + 1}I", rest[:offset_bytes])
477	    dict_section_len = offset_bytes + tentative_offsets[-1]
478	    if dict_section_len > len(rest) - 4 * row_count:
479	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"dictionary overruns payload for {col.name!r}")
480	    dictionary = _decode_utf8_blob(
481	        col, rest[:dict_section_len], dict_size, what="dictionary"
482	    )
483	    index_bytes = rest[dict_section_len:]
484	    if len(index_bytes) != 4 * row_count:
485	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"bad dictionary index length for {col.name!r}")
486	    raw_indices = struct.unpack(f"<{row_count}i", index_bytes) if row_count else ()
487	    values: list[str] = []
488	    for i, idx in enumerate(raw_indices):
489	        is_valid = validity is None or bool((validity[i >> 3] >> (i & 7)) & 1)
490	        if idx == -1:
491	            if not col.nullable or is_valid:
492	                raise ColumnarFormatError(
493	                    f"NULL dictionary index contradicts validity in {col.name!r} row {i}"
494	                )
495	            values.append("")  # replaced with None via validity bitmap below
496	        elif not 0 <= idx < dict_size:
497	            raise ColumnarFormatError(
498	                f"dictionary index {idx} out of range in {col.name!r} row {i}"
499	            )
500	        else:
501	            if not is_valid:
502	                raise ColumnarFormatError(
503	                    f"valid dictionary index in NULL slot of {col.name!r} row {i}"
504	                )
505	            values.append(dictionary[idx])
506	    return values
507

509	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
510	# Header (JSON metadata)
511	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
512	
513	
514	def _stats_json(value: Any) -> Any:
515	    return value
516	
517	
518	def _build_header(
519	    table: Table,
520	    compression: str,
521	    data_section: bytes,
522	    raw_section: bytes,
523	    chunk_info: Sequence[dict],
524	) -> dict:
525	    return {
526	        "compression": compression,
527	        "row_count": table.row_count,
528	        "data_length": len(data_section),
529	        "data_crc32": zlib.crc32(data_section) & 0xFFFFFFFF,
530	        "uncompressed_length": len(raw_section),
531	        "columns": list(chunk_info),
532	    }
533	
534	
535	def _dump_json(header: dict) -> bytes:
536	    return json.dumps(
537	        header, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False
538	    ).encode("utf-8")
539	
540	
541	def _reject_duplicate_keys(pairs: Sequence[tuple[str, Any]]) -> dict:
542	    seen: set[str] = set()
543	    for key, _ in pairs:
544	        if key in seen:
545	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"duplicate JSON key in header: {key!r}")
546	        seen.add(key)
547	    return dict(pairs)
548	
549	
550	def _reject_json_constant(value: str):
551	    raise ColumnarFormatError(f"illegal JSON constant in header: {value}")
552	
553	
554	def _is_uint32(value: Any) -> bool:
555	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and 0 <= value <= 0xFFFFFFFF
556	
557	
558	def _is_nonneg_int(value: Any) -> bool:
559	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 0
560	
561	
562	def _validate_header(header: Any) -> dict:
563	    if not isinstance(header, dict):
564	        raise ColumnarFormatError("header must be a JSON object")
565	    unknown = set(header) - _HEADER_KEYS
566	    if unknown:
567	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"unknown header key(s): {sorted(unknown)!r}")
568	    compression = header.get("compression")
569	    if compression not in _COMPRESSION_NAMES:
570	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"unknown compression in header: {compression!r}")
571	    row_count = header.get("row_count")
572	    if not _is_nonneg_int(row_count):
573	        raise ColumnarFormatError("header row_count must be a non-negative integer")
574	    data_length = header.get("data_length")
575	    if not _is_nonneg_int(data_length):
576	        raise ColumnarFormatError("header data_length must be a non-negative integer")
577	    data_crc = header.get("data_crc32")
578	    if not _is_uint32(data_crc):
579	        raise ColumnarFormatError("header data_crc32 must be a uint32")
580	    uncompressed_length = header.get("uncompressed_length")
581	    if not _is_nonneg_int(uncompressed_length):
582	        raise ColumnarFormatError("header uncompressed_length must be a non-negative integer")
583	    entries = header.get("columns")
584	    if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:
585	        raise ColumnarFormatError("header must list at least one column")
586	
587	    seen: set[str] = set()
588	    next_offset = 0
589	    for pos, entry in enumerate(entries):
590	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
591	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column header #{pos} must be an object")
592	        unknown_col = set(entry) - _COLUMN_KEYS
593	        if unknown_col:
594	            raise ColumnarFormatError(
595	                f"column header #{pos}: unknown key(s) {sorted(unknown_col)!r}"
596	            )
597	        name = entry.get("name")
598	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
599	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column header #{pos}: name must be a non-empty string")
600	        if name in seen:
601	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"duplicate column in header: {name!r}")
602	        seen.add(name)
603	        col_type = entry.get("type")
604	        if col_type not in _TYPE_NAMES:
605	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: unknown type {col_type!r}")
606	        nullable = entry.get("nullable")
607	        if not isinstance(nullable, bool):
608	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: nullable must be true or false")
609	        encoding = entry.get("encoding")
610	        if encoding not in _ENCODING_NAMES:
611	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: unknown encoding {encoding!r}")
612	        if encoding == "dictionary" and col_type != "utf8":
613	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: dictionary encoding requires utf8")
614	        for key in ("offset", "length", "null_count"):
615	            if not _is_nonneg_int(entry.get(key)):
616	                raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: {key} must be a non-negative integer")
617	        if not _is_uint32(entry.get("crc32")):
618	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: crc32 must be a uint32")
619	        if "min" not in entry or "max" not in entry:
620	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: min and max keys are required")
621	        if entry["offset"] != next_offset:
622	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: chunks are not contiguous")
623	        next_offset += entry["length"]
624	        null_count = entry["null_count"]
625	        if null_count > row_count:
626	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: null_count exceeds row_count")
627	        if not nullable and null_count:
628	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: NULL count set for non-nullable column")
629	        _validate_stats(entry, col_type, row_count, null_count)
630	    if next_offset != uncompressed_length:
631	        raise ColumnarFormatError("declared uncompressed length does not match column chunks")
632	    return header
633	
634	
635	def _validate_stats(
636	    entry: dict, col_type: str, row_count: int, null_count: int
637	) -> None:
638	    name = entry["name"]
639	    minimum = entry.get("min")
640	    maximum = entry.get("max")
641	    if null_count == row_count:
642	        if minimum is not None or maximum is not None:
643	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: all-NULL column needs null min/max")
644	        return
645	    if minimum is None or maximum is None:
646	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: min and max must both be present")
647	    if col_type == "bool":
648	        if not isinstance(minimum, bool) or not isinstance(maximum, bool):
649	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: bool stats must be booleans")
650	    elif col_type == "int64":
651	        if not _is_int64_json(minimum) or not _is_int64_json(maximum):
652	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: int64 stats must be int64 integers")
653	    elif col_type == "float64":
654	        if not _is_finite_json_float(minimum) or not _is_finite_json_float(maximum):
655	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: float64 stats must be finite numbers")
656	        minimum = float(minimum)
657	        maximum = float(maximum)
658	    elif col_type == "utf8":
659	        if not isinstance(minimum, str) or not isinstance(maximum, str):
660	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: utf8 stats must be strings")
661	    if minimum > maximum:
662	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: min exceeds max")
663	
664	
665	def _is_int64_json(value: Any) -> bool:
666	    return (
667	        isinstance(value, int)
668	        and not isinstance(value, bool)
669	        and -(2**63) <= value <= 2**63 - 1
670	    )
671	
672	
673	def _is_finite_json_float(value: Any) -> bool:
674	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
675	        return False
676	    value = float(value)
677	    return value == value and value not in (float("inf"), float("-inf"))
678	
679	
680	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
681	# Writing
682	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
683	
684	
685	def write_file(
686	    path: str | os.PathLike,
687	    table: Table,
688	    *,
689	    compression: str = "none",
690	    dictionary_encoding: Sequence[str] = (),
691	) -> None:
692	    """Write ``table`` to ``path`` deterministically and atomically.
693	
694	    All validation happens before any file is created, so invalid arguments
695	    never create or alter the destination.
696	    """
697	    if not isinstance(table, Table):
698	        raise TypeError("table must be a Table instance")
699	    if compression not in _COMPRESSION_NAMES:
700	        raise ValueError(f"unknown compression: {compression!r}")
701	    if isinstance(dictionary_encoding, str):
702	        raise ValueError("dictionary_encoding must be a sequence of column names")
703	    dict_names = tuple(dictionary_encoding)
704	    if len(set(dict_names)) != len(dict_names):
705	        raise ValueError("dictionary_encoding contains duplicate column names")
706	    unknown = [name for name in dict_names if name not in table.schema.names]
707	    if unknown:
708	        raise ValueError(f"dictionary_encoding references unknown column(s): {unknown!r}")
709	    for name in dict_names:
710	        col = table.schema.columns[table.schema.index(name)]
711	        if col.type != "utf8":
712	            raise ValueError(
713	                f"dictionary encoding is only valid for utf8 columns, not {col.name!r} ({col.type})"
714	            )
715	    dict_set = set(dict_names)
716	
717	    raw_section = bytearray()
718	    chunk_info: list[dict] = []
719	    for i, col in enumerate(table.schema.columns):
720	        values = table._columns[i]
721	        payload, null_count, minimum, maximum = _encode_payload(
722	            col, values, use_dictionary=col.name in dict_set
723	        )
724	        chunk_info.append(
725	            {
726	                "name": col.name,
727	                "type": col.type,
728	                "nullable": col.nullable,
729	                "encoding": "dictionary" if col.name in dict_set else "plain",
730	                "offset": len(raw_section),
731	                "length": len(payload),
732	                "crc32": zlib.crc32(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF,
733	                "null_count": null_count,
734	                "min": _stats_json(minimum),
735	                "max": _stats_json(maximum),
736	            }
737	        )
738	        raw_section.extend(payload)
739	
740	    if compression == "zlib":
741	        data_section = zlib.compress(bytes(raw_section), level=6)
742	    else:
743	        data_section = bytes(raw_section)
744	    header = _build_header(table, compression, data_section, bytes(raw_section), chunk_info)
745	    header_bytes = _dump_json(header)
746	    if len(header_bytes) > _MAX_HEADER_BYTES:
747	        raise ValueError("serialized header exceeds the size limit")
748	
749	    prefix = _MAGIC + bytes([FORMAT_VERSION]) + struct.pack("<I", len(header_bytes))
750	    body = prefix + header_bytes + data_section
751	    crc = zlib.crc32(body) & 0xFFFFFFFF
752	    blob = body + struct.pack("<I", crc) + _FOOTER_MARKER
753	
754	    _atomic_write(path, blob)
755	
756	
757	def _atomic_write(path: str | os.PathLike, blob: bytes) -> None:
758	    path = os.fspath(path)
759	    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
760	    fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".columnar-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory)
761	    try:
762	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
763	            handle.write(blob)
764	            handle.flush()
765	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
766	        os.replace(tmp_name, path)
767	    except BaseException:
768	        try:
769	            os.unlink(tmp_name)
770	        except FileNotFoundError:
771	            pass
772	        raise
773	
774	
775	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
776	# Reading
777	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
778	
779	
780	def _read_exact(handle, size: int, what: str) -> bytes:
781	    data = handle.read(size)
782	    if len(data) != size:
783	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"truncated file while reading {what}")
784	    return data
785	
786	
787	def _read_header(path: str | os.PathLike) -> tuple[bytes, bytes, dict, int]:
788	    """Read prefix + JSON header and fstat the declared total size.
789	
790	    Metadata-only: no data bytes are touched. Returns the raw prefix, raw
791	    header bytes, the validated header dict and the on-disk file size.
792	    """
793	    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
794	        prefix = handle.read(_PREFIX_LEN)
795	        if len(prefix) < _PREFIX_LEN:
796	            if not prefix:
797	                raise ColumnarFormatError("empty file")
798	            if len(prefix) >= 4 and prefix[:4] != _MAGIC:
799	                raise ColumnarFormatError("bad magic number")
800	            raise ColumnarFormatError("truncated file prefix")
801	        if prefix[:4] != _MAGIC:
802	            raise ColumnarFormatError("bad magic number")
803	        version = prefix[4]
804	        if version != FORMAT_VERSION:
805	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"unsupported format version: {version}")
806	        (header_length,) = struct.unpack("<I", prefix[5:9])
807	        if header_length == 0 or header_length > _MAX_HEADER_BYTES:
808	            raise ColumnarFormatError("header length out of bounds")
809	        header_bytes = _read_exact(handle, header_length, "header")
810	        actual_size = os.fstat(handle.fileno()).st_size
811	
812	    try:
813	        header = json.loads(
814	            header_bytes.decode("utf-8"),
815	            object_pairs_hook=_reject_duplicate_keys,
816	            parse_constant=_reject_json_constant,
817	        )
818	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
819	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"invalid header JSON: {exc}") from None
820	    header = _validate_header(header)
821	
822	    expected_size = _PREFIX_LEN + header_length + header["data_length"] + _FOOTER_LEN
823	    if actual_size != expected_size:
824	        raise ColumnarFormatError(
825	            f"file size {actual_size} does not match declared size {expected_size}"
826	        )
827	    return prefix, header_bytes, header, actual_size
828	
829	
830	def read_file(
831	    path: str | os.PathLike, *, columns: Sequence[str] | None = None
832	) -> Table:
833	    """Read a table, optionally projecting ``columns`` in the given order."""
834	    prefix, header_bytes, header, _ = _read_header(path)
835	    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
836	        handle.seek(_PREFIX_LEN + len(header_bytes))
837	        data_section = _read_exact(handle, header["data_length"], "data section")
838	        footer = _read_exact(handle, _FOOTER_LEN, "footer")
839	        if handle.read(1):
840	            raise ColumnarFormatError("trailing bytes after footer")
841	
842	    (footer_crc,) = struct.unpack("<I", footer[:4])
843	    if footer[4:] != _FOOTER_MARKER:
844	        raise ColumnarFormatError("bad end marker")
845	    covered = prefix + header_bytes + data_section
846	    if (zlib.crc32(covered) & 0xFFFFFFFF) != footer_crc:
847	        raise ColumnarFormatError("overall checksum mismatch")
848	    raw_section = _inflate(header, data_section)
849	
850	    schema_cols = []
851	    decoded_columns = []
852	    for entry in header["columns"]:
853	        col = ColumnSchema(entry["name"], entry["type"], entry["nullable"])
854	        schema_cols.append(col)
855	        start = entry["offset"]
856	        end = start + entry["length"]
857	        if end > len(raw_section):
858	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {col.name!r}: chunk outside data section")
859	        payload = raw_section[start:end]
860	        if (zlib.crc32(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF) != entry["crc32"]:
861	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {col.name!r}: checksum mismatch")
862	        values = _decode_column(col, entry["encoding"], header["row_count"], payload)
863	        _verify_stats(col, values, entry)
864	        decoded_columns.append(values)
865	
866	    schema = Schema(schema_cols)
867	    table = Table._from_storage(schema, decoded_columns)
868	    if columns is not None:
869	        table = table.project(columns)
870	    return table
871	
872	
873	def _inflate(header: dict, data_section: bytes) -> bytes:
874	    if (zlib.crc32(data_section) & 0xFFFFFFFF) != header["data_crc32"]:
875	        raise ColumnarFormatError("data section checksum mismatch")
876	    if header["compression"] == "zlib":
877	        try:
878	            raw_section = zlib.decompress(data_section)
879	        except zlib.error as exc:
880	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"cannot decompress data section: {exc}") from None
881	    else:
882	        raw_section = data_section
883	    if len(raw_section) != header["uncompressed_length"]:
884	        raise ColumnarFormatError("uncompressed data length mismatch")
885	    return raw_section
886	
887	
888	def _verify_stats(col: ColumnSchema, values: Sequence, entry: dict) -> None:
889	    null_count = sum(1 for value in values if value is None)
890	    if null_count != entry["null_count"]:
891	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {col.name!r}: null_count mismatch")
892	    present = [value for value in values if value is not None]
893	    if not present:
894	        if entry["min"] is not None or entry["max"] is not None:
895	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {col.name!r}: stats mismatch")
896	        return
897	    minimum = min(present)
898	    maximum = max(present)
899	    meta_min = entry["min"]
900	    meta_max = entry["max"]
901	    if col.type == "float64":
902	        meta_min = float(meta_min)
903	        meta_max = float(meta_max)
904	    if minimum != meta_min or maximum != meta_max:
905	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {col.name!r}: min/max mismatch")
906	
907	
908	def inspect_file(path: str | os.PathLike) -> dict:
909	    """Read only the file metadata; no data bytes are read, decompressed or decoded.
910	
911	    Returns a dict with fixed key order: ``format_version``, ``row_count``,
912	    ``columns``; columns stay in schema order, each with keys ``name``,
913	    ``type``, ``nullable``, ``row_count``, ``null_count``, ``min``, ``max``.
914	    """
915	    _, _, header, _ = _read_header(path)
916	    return {
917	        "format_version": FORMAT_VERSION,
918	        "row_count": header["row_count"],
919	        "columns": [
920	            {
921	                "name": entry["name"],
922	                "type": entry["type"],
923	                "nullable": entry["nullable"],
924	                "row_count": header["row_count"],
925	                "null_count": entry["null_count"],
926	                "min": entry["min"],
927	                "max": entry["max"],
928	            }
929	            for entry in header["columns"]
930	        ],
931	    }

content.content:
1	"""Single-file SQL query layer.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	* :func:`query_file` -- run a ``SELECT ... FROM input [WHERE ...]`` query
6	  against one columnar file and return a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table`
7	* :func:`query_files` -- run a statement against a table-name to path
8	  mapping, optionally chaining several equi-joins
9	* :func:`explain_file` / :func:`explain_files` -- parse, bind and plan the
10	  same statements without executing them; only file metadata is read
11	* :class:`QuerySyntaxError` -- lexical / grammatical errors
12	* :class:`QueryValidationError` -- unknown columns, wrong table name,
13	  type-incompatible comparisons, invalid aggregate use
14	
15	The accepted grammar (keywords case-insensitive)::
16	
17	    query       := SELECT [DISTINCT] select_item (',' select_item)*
18	                   FROM ident [WHERE expr] [GROUP BY ident (',' ident)*]
19	                   [HAVING expr]
20	                   [ORDER BY order_item (',' order_item)*]
21	                   [LIMIT uint]
22	    select_item := '*' | ident | agg_name '(' [DISTINCT] ('*' | ident) ')'
23	                   | scalar_expr AS alias
24	    order_item  := (ident | agg_name '(' [DISTINCT] ('*' | ident) ')')
25	                   [ASC | DESC] [NULLS FIRST | NULLS LAST]
26	    expr       := or_expr
27	    or_expr     := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
28	    and_expr    := cmp_expr (AND cmp_expr)*
29	    cmp_expr    := not_factor (cmp_op not_factor)?
30	    not_factor  := NOT not_factor | postfix
31	    postfix     := scalar_expr (IS [NOT] NULL)?
32	    scalar_expr := term (('+' | '-') term)*
33	    term        := factor (('*' | '/') factor)*
34	    factor      := ('+' | '-') factor | atom
35	    atom        := '(' expr ')' | operand
36	                | CASE WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr
37	                  (WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr)*
38	                  (ELSE scalar_expr)? END
39	    operand     := ident | literal
40	    literal     := TRUE | FALSE | [+-]? int64 | [+-]? finite float64
41	                   | single-quoted utf8
42	
43	The supported aggregates are ``COUNT(*)``, ``COUNT(ident)`` and
44	``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` applied to one column.  Each of
45	``COUNT`` / ``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` also accepts
46	``DISTINCT`` before its single column argument (``COUNT(DISTINCT ident)``
47	etc.): rows are first selected by WHERE, then within each group (or the
48	single global group) NULL arguments are ignored and the remaining values
49	are deduplicated by the column's type -- float64 ``0.0`` and ``-0.0``
50	count as the same value -- before the aggregate runs.  ``COUNT(DISTINCT
51	x)`` returns the number of distinct non-NULL values (0 on empty input,
52	a non-nullable int64); the other DISTINCT aggregates return NULL when no
53	distinct non-NULL value remains and otherwise keep the result type,
54	nullability, comparison rules and overflow / non-finite
55	:class:`QueryValidationError` behaviour of their plain counterparts.
56	DISTINCT here only deduplicates the aggregate's argument values; it does
57	not change ``SELECT DISTINCT`` row deduplication, and the argument stays
58	a single column reference (no ``*``, expressions, multiple arguments or
59	nested aggregates).  A misplaced DISTINCT keyword, a missing argument,
60	``*``, an expression or multiple arguments inside a DISTINCT call raise
61	:class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is opened.  DISTINCT
62	aggregates may appear wherever plain aggregates may (SELECT, HAVING,
63	ORDER BY), and textually identical calls share one computation.  Without
64	GROUP BY the projection may contain aggregate expressions only; with
65	GROUP BY it may additionally contain the grouped columns.  A bare ``*``
66	must not be mixed with aggregates or grouping.  Aggregates are not
67	allowed inside WHERE, may not be nested, and aliases are not supported
68	for bare columns or aggregate calls.
69	
70	Scalar arithmetic (parentheses, unary ``+``/``-``, binary ``+`` ``-``
71	``*`` ``/``; precedence: parentheses, unary, ``*``/``/``, ``+``/``-``)
72	is available over int64 / float64 columns and numeric literals in SELECT
73	and WHERE.  A computed SELECT expression must be named with ``AS`` (the
74	alias follows the usual identifier rules and must be unique among the
75	output names); bare columns and aggregate calls keep their existing
76	result names.  int64 ``+``/``-``/``*`` on two int64 operands yields
77	int64; any float64 operand or a division yields float64, and unary
78	operators preserve the operand type.  Any NULL operand makes the result
79	NULL; the output column is nullable iff a participating column is
80	nullable (pure constants are not).  int64 overflow, division by zero and
81	non-finite float64 results raise :class:`QueryValidationError`.  A
82	numeric expression used directly as a boolean condition is rejected with
83	:class:`QueryValidationError` as well.  Non-aggregate queries execute
84	WHERE, then compute the sort keys, stably sort, apply LIMIT and only
85	then evaluate the SELECT expressions, so filtered or truncated rows
86	never trigger division-by-zero or overflow in the projection; a
87	DISTINCT query instead evaluates the projection right after WHERE,
88	deduplicates the result rows, and only then sorts and applies LIMIT.  ORDER BY
89	may name a SELECT alias (an alias shadows an input column of the same
90	name) and sorts on the expression's result type with the usual NULL
91	placement and stability rules.  Aggregate queries do not accept scalar
92	expressions: GROUP BY keys and aggregate arguments stay plain column
93	references, and mixing a scalar expression into an aggregate query
94	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
95	
96	``SELECT DISTINCT`` removes duplicate rows from a non-aggregate query:
97	the projection may be a star, plain columns or ``AS``-aliased scalar
98	expressions exactly as without DISTINCT, and deduplication compares the
99	full projected result row column by column after WHERE.  Two NULLs in
100	the same result column compare equal, NULL never equals a non-NULL
101	value, bool / utf8 / numeric values keep their existing comparison
102	semantics, and float64 ``0.0`` and ``-0.0`` compare equal.  Without
103	ORDER BY the surviving rows keep the order of the first occurrence of
104	each distinct result row; ORDER BY then sorts the deduplicated rows and
105	LIMIT keeps the first N.  The projection expressions are evaluated
106	only for rows that passed WHERE (and, with ORDER BY, before the sort),
107	so a division by zero, int64 overflow or non-finite float64 result that
108	actually occurs still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.  ORDER BY
109	of a DISTINCT query may name only bare columns or explicit aliases that
110	are part of the projection; an unprojected or otherwise unknown name
111	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`, and the sort direction, NULL
112	placement and stability rules are unchanged.  DISTINCT combined with
113	GROUP BY, HAVING or any aggregate projection raises
114	:class:`QueryValidationError`; argument-level ``DISTINCT`` inside an
115	aggregate call (``COUNT(DISTINCT ...)`` etc.) is a separate feature
116	described above and stays an aggregate query.  A missing projection, a
117	repeated DISTINCT or a misplaced DISTINCT keyword raises
118	:class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is opened.
119	
120	Searched CASE expressions
121	(``CASE WHEN cond THEN result [WHEN ...] [ELSE result] END``; the simple
122	``CASE value WHEN ...`` form is not supported and at least one WHEN is
123	required) are scalar operands and may be nested inside more arithmetic,
124	comparisons and other CASE expressions.  For each row the WHEN conditions
125	are tested in written order and only TRUE matches; FALSE and UNKNOWN fall
126	through, an explicit ELSE supplies the fallback and a missing ELSE yields
127	NULL.  Only the chosen result is evaluated, so division by zero, int64
128	overflow or a non-finite float64 inside an unhit branch never raises; a
129	chosen result that errors still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
130	Every reachable THEN and an explicit ELSE must share one type family:
131	int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64, while bool and utf8 must
132	match each other exactly (any other mix raises
133	:class:`QueryValidationError`).  The result column is nullable if any
134	reachable result is nullable or the ELSE is omitted.  WHEN conditions use
135	the same boolean type check and three-valued logic as WHERE; CASE stays a
136	scalar expression, so it is rejected in aggregate arguments, GROUP BY and
137	the projection of an aggregate query just like the other scalar
138	expressions.
139	
140	Operator precedence (highest first) is NOT, comparison, AND, OR; IS [NOT]
141	NULL is a postfix of its scalar operand.  Comparison operands may be
142	column references, literals or scalar arithmetic expressions.  WHERE
143	follows SQL three-valued logic: a normal
144	comparison against NULL yields UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN propagates through the
145	logical operators, and only TRUE rows are returned.
146	
147	After WHERE, rows are grouped in GROUP BY column order (a NULL key forms
148	its own group); without an explicit ORDER BY groups come out in the order
149	of their first selected row.  An optional HAVING clause between GROUP BY
150	and ORDER BY filters the formed groups with the same boolean expression
151	grammar and three-valued logic as WHERE: its conditions combine grouping
152	columns, aggregate calls and type-compatible literals with NOT / AND / OR
153	/ comparisons / IS [NOT] NULL, only groups whose condition is TRUE are
154	kept, and aggregates named in HAVING need not appear in SELECT.  Without
155	GROUP BY HAVING filters the single global aggregate row (still produced
156	when WHERE selected no rows); with GROUP BY an empty selection yields
157	zero groups.  HAVING may not name ungrouped plain columns, ``*``, CASE,
158	scalar arithmetic or nested aggregates; it is rejected on a completely
159	non-aggregate query.  ORDER BY may only name a selected result; ASC is the
160	default, NULLs sort last regardless of direction unless NULLS FIRST /
161	NULLS LAST is given, and groups equal on every sort key keep that
162	first-row order.  LIMIT then keeps the first N groups.  Without GROUP BY
163	and aggregates an aggregate query over zero selected rows still yields one
164	output row (COUNT 0, the other aggregates NULL), unless HAVING removes it;
165	with GROUP BY it yields zero rows.
166	
167	Multi-file queries (:func:`query_files`) add a deterministic chain of zero
168	or more equi-joins to the grammar::
169	
170	    query := SELECT ... FROM from_table
171	             { join_kind JOIN next_table
172	               ON (earlier_table.col = next_table.col
173	                   | next_table.col = earlier_table.col) } ...
174	    join_kind := INNER | LEFT | RIGHT | FULL OUTER
175	
176	``sources`` maps table names to file paths; only the tables referenced by
177	the statement are read.  Each join step introduces exactly one not-yet-used
178	table (aliases and repeated tables are rejected) and its single ON equality
179	connects a qualified column of that new table with a qualified column of any
180	table introduced earlier (FROM or a previous join); the two sides of the
181	equality are interchangeable.  Compound or non-equality ON conditions,
182	other join types and ``FULL`` without ``OUTER`` are syntax errors raised
183	before any file is opened.  In any statement that contains a JOIN every
184	column reference outside ``COUNT(*)`` must be qualified as ``table.column``
185	(either part may be a double-quoted identifier).  ``SELECT *`` emits the
186	referenced schemas in FROM/JOIN order with ``table.column`` names; explicit
187	projections keep their qualified names and aggregates keep the uppercase
188	``FUNC(table.column)`` labels.
189	
190	Each step is evaluated with the materialised intermediate result as its
191	left input and the newly read table as its right input.  Join keys may
192	share a type or mix int64 with float64; NULL keys never match.  INNER JOIN
193	emits every matching combination, LEFT JOIN also emits unmatched left rows
194	with the right-side values set to NULL (the new table's result columns are
195	nullable), RIGHT JOIN emits all new-table rows in new-file order (one new
196	row's matches expand in intermediate/current row order) padding the whole
197	intermediate side with NULL (every earlier table's result columns become
198	nullable), and FULL OUTER JOIN emits the LEFT JOIN output and then appends
199	the unmatched new rows in new-file order (every result column is nullable).
200	INNER / LEFT / FULL expand in the current intermediate row order, with the
201	matching new rows in new-file order within one current row; RIGHT expands
202	in new-file row order with the matches in current row order.  Nullability
203	is derived per step: once a step makes an earlier table's columns
204	nullable, later steps keep them nullable.  WHERE / GROUP BY / HAVING /
205	projection / DISTINCT / stable sorting / LIMIT run only after the whole
206	chain has been built, with their usual semantics.
207	
208	The multi-file entry points (:func:`query_files`, :func:`explain_files`)
209	take an optional ``join_strategy`` of ``"hash"`` or ``"sort_merge"``; an
210	explicit strategy is applied to every join step.  Both strategies accept
211	the same statements and return identical column descriptions, values, NULL
212	placement and row order; they differ only in how matching right rows are
213	located (a right-key hash index versus sorting both sides on the key and
214	merging equal-key runs).  With the argument omitted the historical
215	default join path is used and the explain plan carries no strategy field;
216	with an explicit strategy every plan Join operator gains a ``strategy``
217	field of ``HASH`` or ``SORT_MERGE``.  A JOIN-less statement accepts either
218	strategy but gains no extra operator, and an invalid strategy raises
219	:class:`ValueError` before any source file is opened.
220	
221	The explain plan lists the referenced sources and their Scan operators in
222	FROM/JOIN order with ``required_columns`` attributed to each source, then
223	one Join operator per step in the same order, recording the step type and
224	the two normalised qualified keys (the earlier table on the left, the
225	freshly introduced table on the right).
226	"""

300	def _validate_join_strategy(join_strategy: Any) -> str | None:
301	    """Validate the optional ``join_strategy`` argument.
302	
303	    Returns the canonical lowercase strategy name, or ``None`` when the
304	    caller did not request one.  Any other value (including a non-string)
305	    raises :class:`ValueError`; callers run this before opening any file.
306	    """
307	    if join_strategy is None:
308	        return None
309	    if not isinstance(join_strategy, str) or join_strategy not in _JOIN_STRATEGIES:
310	        allowed = ", ".join(sorted(_JOIN_STRATEGIES))
311	        raise ValueError(
312	            f"invalid join_strategy: {join_strategy!r}; expected one of {allowed}"
313	        )
314	    return join_strategy

330	@dataclass(frozen=True)
331	class _Token:
332	    kind: str  # one of: keyword, ident, number, string, op, star, eof
333	    value: Any
334	    text: str
335	
336	
337	_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(
338	    r"""
339	    \d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?   # 1, 1., 1.5, 1e3, 1.5e-2
340	    | \.\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?         # .5
341	    """,
342	    re.VERBOSE,
343	)
344	# Bare identifiers: Unicode letters/underscore first, then word characters.
345	_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W\d]\w*", re.UNICODE)
346	
347	
348	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> list[_Token]:
349	    if not isinstance(sql, str):
350	        raise QuerySyntaxError("SQL statement must be a string")
351	    tokens: list[_Token] = []
352	    i = 0
353	    n = len(sql)
354	    while i < n:
355	        ch = sql[i]
356	        if ch.isspace():
357	            i += 1
358	            continue
359	        if ch == "*":
360	            tokens.append(_Token("star", None, ch))
361	            i += 1
362	            continue
363	        if ch in ",()+-/":
364	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
365	            i += 1
366	            continue
367	        if ch in "=<>!":
368	            if ch == "!" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
369	                tokens.append(_Token("op", "!=", "!="))
370	                i += 2
371	                continue
372	            if ch in "<>" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
373	                op = ch + "="
374	                tokens.append(_Token("op", op, op))
375	                i += 2
376	                continue
377	            if ch in "=<>":
378	                tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
379	                i += 1
380	                continue
381	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
382	        if ch == "'":
383	            value, new_i = _tokenize_string(sql, i)
384	            tokens.append(_Token("string", value, sql[i:new_i]))
385	            i = new_i
386	            continue
387	        if ch == '"':
388	            value, new_i = _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql, i)
389	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(value, quoted=True))
390	            i = new_i
391	            continue
392	        if ch.isdigit() or ch == ".":
393	            match = _NUMBER_RE.match(sql, i)
394	            if match:
395	                text = match.group(0)
396	                tokens.append(_Token("number", _parse_number(text), text))
397	                i = match.end()
398	                continue
399	            # A '.' that does not start a number is the qualifier separator
400	            # used by multi-table queries ("table.column").
401	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ".", ch))
402	            i += 1
403	            continue
404	        match = _IDENT_RE.match(sql, i)
405	        if match:
406	            text = match.group(0)
407	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(text, quoted=False))
408	            i = match.end()
409	            continue
410	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at position {i}")
411	    tokens.append(_Token("eof", None, ""))
412	    return tokens
413	
414	
415	def _token_from_word(word: str, *, quoted: bool) -> _Token:
416	    lowered = word.lower()
417	    if not quoted and lowered in _KEYWORDS:
418	        if lowered == "true":
419	            return _Token("number", True, word)
420	        if lowered == "false":
421	            return _Token("number", False, word)
422	        return _Token("keyword", lowered, word)
423	    return _Token("qident" if quoted else "ident", word, word)
424	
425	
426	def _tokenize_string(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
427	    parts: list[str] = []
428	    i = start + 1
429	    n = len(sql)
430	    while True:
431	        j = sql.find("'", i)
432	        if j == -1:
433	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated string literal")
434	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
435	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == "'":
436	            parts.append("'")
437	            i = j + 2
438	            continue
439	        value = "".join(parts)
440	        try:
441	            value.encode("utf-8")
442	        except UnicodeEncodeError:
443	            raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal is not valid UTF-8") from None
444	        return value, j + 1
445	
446	
447	def _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
448	    parts: list[str] = []
449	    i = start + 1
450	    n = len(sql)
451	    while True:
452	        j = sql.find('"', i)
453	        if j == -1:
454	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated quoted identifier")
455	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
456	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == '"':
457	            parts.append('"')
458	            i = j + 2
459	            continue
460	        value = "".join(parts)
461	        if not value:
462	            raise QuerySyntaxError("quoted identifier must not be empty")
463	        return value, j + 1
464	
465	
466	def _parse_number(text: str) -> int | float:
467	    try:
468	        if any(ch in text for ch in ".eE"):
469	            value: int | float = float(text)
470	        else:
471	            value = int(text, 10)
472	    except ValueError:
473	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}") from None
474	    if isinstance(value, int):
475	        # The magnitude 2**63 is accepted unsigned; the signed range check
476	        # happens after the optional leading sign is applied.
477	        if not (0 <= value <= 2**63):
478	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"integer literal {text} is outside the int64 range")
479	        return value
480	    if not math.isfinite(value):
481	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"float literal {text} must be finite")
482	    return value

487	#
488	# Node tuples:
489	#   ("literal", python_value, type_name)
490	#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)        -- as parsed
491	#   ("column", name, index, type_name, nullable)      -- after binding
492	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node)              -- as parsed (+ - * /)
493	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node, type_name)   -- after binding
494	#   ("unary", operand, negate)                        -- as parsed
495	#   ("unary", operand, negate, type_name)             -- after binding
496	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None)   -- as parsed
497	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None, type_name) -- after binding
498	#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
499	#   ("isnull", operand, negate)
500	#   ("not", operand)
501	#   ("and"|"or", left, right)
502	# Predicate nodes are boolean-typed (three-valued at evaluation time);
503	# "literal"/"column"/"arith"/"unary" nodes are value nodes.
504	#
505	# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:
506	#   ("column_ref", name)                 -- a plain column name
507	#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'
508	#   ("expr", alias)                      -- a computed scalar expression

521	    expr: tuple | None = None  # parsed scalar expression for kind == "expr"

535	    A statement may chain several steps in FROM/JOIN order; each step takes
536	    the intermediate result built so far as its left input and one freshly
537	    introduced table as its right input.
538	    """
539	
540	    kind: str  # "inner" | "left" | "right" | "full"
541	    table: str  # right table name as spelled
542	    table_quoted: bool

548	class _Select:
549	    items: tuple[_RefItem, ...]  # projection; may be a single ("star",) item
550	    table: str
551	    table_quoted: bool
552	    where: tuple | None
553	    # GROUP BY entries are (table|None, table_quoted, name) triples.

560	    joins: tuple[_Join, ...] = ()
561	    # SELECT DISTINCT: deduplicate the projected rows (non-aggregate only).
562	    distinct: bool = False
563	
564	    @property
565	    def star(self) -> bool:
566	        return len(self.items) == 1 and self.items[0].kind == "star"
567	
568	    @property
569	    def has_aggregate(self) -> bool:
570	        return any(item.kind == "agg" for item in self.items)
571	
572	    @property
573	    def is_aggregate_query(self) -> bool:
574	        return self.has_aggregate or self.group_by is not None or self.having is not None

577	class _Parser:
578	    _CMP_OPS = frozenset(("=", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="))
579	
580	    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):
581	        self.tokens = tokens
582	        self.pos = 0
583	        # Multi-table statements (qualified names + join clauses) are only
584	        # enabled for query_files; single-file entry points keep rejecting
585	        # them as syntax errors.
586	        self._allow_join = allow_join
587	
588	    def parse(self) -> _Select:
589	        select = self._parse_select()
590	        if self._peek().kind != "eof":
591	            tok = self._peek()
592	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected trailing input {tok.text!r}")
593	        return select

595	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:
596	        self._expect_keyword("select")
597	        distinct = self._accept_keyword("distinct")
598	        items = tuple(self._parse_projection())
599	        self._expect_keyword("from")
600	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
601	        joins: tuple[_Join, ...] = ()
602	        if self._allow_join:
603	            joins = tuple(self._parse_join_clauses())
604	        where = None
605	        if self._accept_keyword("where"):
606	            where = self._parse_or()
607	        group_by = None
608	        if self._accept_keyword("group"):
609	            self._expect_keyword("by")
610	            names = [self._parse_group_name()]
611	            while self._accept_op(","):
612	                names.append(self._parse_group_name())
613	            group_by = tuple(names)
614	        having = None
615	        if self._accept_keyword("having"):
616	            having = self._parse_having_or()
617	        order_by = None
618	        if self._accept_keyword("order"):
619	            self._expect_keyword("by")
620	            order_items = [self._parse_order_item()]
621	            while self._accept_op(","):
622	                order_items.append(self._parse_order_item())
623	            order_by = tuple(order_items)
624	        limit = None
625	        if self._accept_keyword("limit"):
626	            limit = self._parse_limit()
627	        return _Select(
628	            items=items,
629	            table=table_tok.value,
630	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
631	            where=where,
632	            group_by=group_by,
633	            having=having,
634	            order_by=order_by,
635	            limit=limit,
636	            joins=joins,
637	            distinct=distinct,
638	        )

640	    def _parse_join_clauses(self) -> list[_Join]:
641	        # Zero or more join clauses may follow FROM; each introduces exactly
642	        # one new table with a single equi-ON condition.  "right" / "full" /
643	        # "outer" stay ordinary identifiers away from this clause (they are
644	        # matched with _accept_word), so columns carrying those names keep
645	        # working outside join parsing.
646	        joins: list[_Join] = []
647	        while True:
648	            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
649	                self._expect_keyword("join")
650	                joins.append(self._parse_join("inner"))
651	            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
652	                self._expect_keyword("join")
653	                joins.append(self._parse_join("left"))
654	            elif self._accept_word("right"):
655	                self._expect_keyword("join")
656	                joins.append(self._parse_join("right"))
657	            elif self._accept_word("full"):
658	                # Only the explicit FULL OUTER JOIN spelling is accepted.
659	                self._expect_word("outer")
660	                self._expect_keyword("join")
661	                joins.append(self._parse_join("full"))
662	            else:
663	                return joins

665	    def _parse_join(self, kind: str) -> _Join:
666	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
667	        self._expect_keyword("on")
668	        left_key = self._parse_on_key()
669	        self._expect_op("=")
670	        right_key = self._parse_on_key()
671	        return _Join(
672	            kind=kind,
673	            table=table_tok.value,
674	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
675	            left_key=left_key,
676	            right_key=right_key,
677	        )

679	    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
680	        tok = self._peek()
681	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
682	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
683	                f"ON requires table-qualified columns, got {tok.text!r}"
684	            )
685	        self._next()
686	        if not self._accept_op("."):
687	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
688	                "ON requires table-qualified columns (table.column)"
689	            )
690	        nxt = self._peek()
691	        if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
692	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
693	                f"expected column name after '.' in ON, got {nxt.text!r}"
694	            )
695	        self._next()
696	        return (tok.value, tok.kind == "qident", nxt.value)

698	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
699	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
700	        while self._accept_op(","):
701	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
702	        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
703	        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
704	        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
705	        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
706	        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
707	        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
708	        tok = self._peek()
709	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident") or (
710	            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"
711	        ):
712	            grouped_ahead = any(
713	                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
714	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
715	            )
716	            if any(item.kind == "agg" for item in items) or grouped_ahead:
717	                raise QueryValidationError(
718	                    f"aliases are not supported; unexpected {tok.text!r} after projection item"
719	                )
720	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected FROM, got {tok.text!r}")
721	        return items

723	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
724	        tok = self._peek()
725	        if tok.kind == "star":
726	            self._next()
727	            return _RefItem("star")
728	        if (
729	            tok.kind == "ident"
730	            and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
731	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
732	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
733	        ):
734	            item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
735	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
736	                raise QueryValidationError(
737	                    "aggregate calls cannot be combined with scalar arithmetic"
738	                )
739	            return item
740	        node = self._parse_arith()
741	        if node[0] == "column":
742	            # A bare (possibly parenthesised) column reference keeps its
743	            # existing projection behaviour and needs no alias.
744	            return _RefItem(
745	                "column", name=node[1], table=node[2], table_quoted=node[3]
746	            )
747	        # A computed scalar expression must be named with AS.
748	        self._expect_keyword("as")
749	        alias = self._peek()
750	        if alias.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
751	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
752	                f"AS requires a result name, got {alias.text!r}"
753	            )
754	        self._next()
755	        return _RefItem("expr", name=alias.value, expr=node)
756	
757	    def _arith_op_ahead(self) -> bool:
758	        tok = self._peek()
759	        return tok.kind == "star" or (
760	            tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-", "/")
761	        )

763	    def _parse_order_item(self) -> _RefItem:
764	        item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
765	        descending = False
766	        if self._accept_keyword("asc"):
767	            descending = False
768	        elif self._accept_keyword("desc"):
769	            descending = True
770	        nulls_first: bool | None = None
771	        if self._accept_keyword("nulls"):
772	            if self._accept_keyword("first"):
773	                nulls_first = True
774	            elif self._accept_keyword("last"):
775	                nulls_first = False
776	            else:
777	                tok = self._peek()
778	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
779	                    f"expected FIRST or LAST after NULLS, got {tok.text!r}"
780	                )
781	        return _RefItem(
782	            item.kind,
783	            name=item.name,
784	            func=item.func,
785	            arg=item.arg,
786	            distinct=item.distinct,
787	            descending=descending,
788	            nulls_first=nulls_first,
789	            table=item.table,
790	            table_quoted=item.table_quoted,
791	            arg_table=item.arg_table,

795	    def _qualifier_ahead(self) -> bool:
796	        nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
797	        return nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "."

799	    def _parse_qualified_column(self) -> _RefItem:
800	        # Current token starts "table.column"; consumes all three tokens.
801	        table_tok = self._next()
802	        self._expect_op(".")
803	        name_tok = self._peek()
804	        if name_tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
805	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
806	                f"expected identifier after '.', got {name_tok.text!r}"
807	            )
808	        self._next()
809	        return _RefItem(
810	            "column",
811	            name=name_tok.value,
812	            table=table_tok.value,
813	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
814	        )

816	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
817	        tok = self._peek()
818	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
819	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
820	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
821	            return self._parse_qualified_column()
822	        # A quoted identifier, or a bare word not spelled like an aggregate,
823	        # can only be a plain column reference.
824	        if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
825	            self._next()
826	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
827	        func = tok.value.lower()
828	        self._next()  # consume the function name
829	        if not self._accept_op("("):
830	            # e.g. a column literally named "count" -- the name token is
831	            # already consumed, so it is a plain column reference.
832	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
833	        arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted, distinct = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
834	        self._expect_op(")")

836	            "agg",
837	            func=func.upper(),
838	            arg=arg,
839	            distinct=distinct,
840	            arg_table=arg_table,
841	            arg_table_quoted=arg_table_quoted,
842	        )

844	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
845	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
846	        # table-qualified) identifier, optionally preceded by DISTINCT.
847	        # Returns (name, table, table_quoted, distinct); name "" stands
848	        # for '*'.  DISTINCT only deduplicates the argument values of this
849	        # call; it accepts a single column reference only, and any other
850	        # use (a star, a missing argument, an expression, extra arguments
851	        # or a nested call) is a syntax error raised before any file is
852	        # opened.
853	        tok = self._peek()
854	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
855	            raise QueryValidationError(
856	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not a CASE expression"
857	            )
858	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "distinct":
859	            self._next()
860	            tok = self._peek()
861	            if tok.kind == "star":
862	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
863	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) does not accept '*'"
864	                )
865	            if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
866	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
867	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) requires one column argument, "
868	                    f"got {tok.text!r}"
869	                )
870	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
871	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
872	                name, table, table_quoted = item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted
873	            else:
874	                self._next()
875	                name, table, table_quoted = tok.value, None, False
876	            nxt = self._peek()
877	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
878	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
879	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) argument must be a column name, "
880	                    "not a function call"
881	                )
882	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
883	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
884	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) argument must be a column "
885	                    "reference, not an expression"
886	                )
887	            return (name, table, table_quoted, True)
888	        if tok.kind == "star":
889	            if func != "count":
890	                raise QuerySyntaxError(f"{func.upper()} does not accept '*'")
891	            self._next()
892	            return ("", None, False, False)
893	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
894	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
895	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
896	            )
897	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
898	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
899	            nxt = self._peek()
900	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
901	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
902	                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
903	                )
904	            self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
905	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted, False)
906	        self._next()
907	        nxt = self._peek()
908	        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
909	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
910	                raise QueryValidationError(
911	                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "
912	                    f"{func.upper()}({tok.value.upper()}(...))"
913	                )
914	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
915	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
916	            )
917	        self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
918	        return (tok.value, None, False, False)
919	
920	    def _reject_expression_in_agg_arg(self, func: str) -> None:
921	        # Aggregate arguments stay limited to plain column references; a
922	        # scalar expression inside an aggregate query is a validation error.
923	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
924	            raise QueryValidationError(
925	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not an expression"
926	            )
