928	    def _parse_limit(self) -> int:
929	        tok = self._peek()
930	        if (
931	            tok.kind != "number"
932	            or isinstance(tok.value, bool)
933	            or not isinstance(tok.value, int)
934	        ):
935	            raise QuerySyntaxError("LIMIT requires an unsigned integer literal")
936	        self._next()
937	        if not (0 <= tok.value <= 2**63 - 1):
938	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
939	                f"LIMIT value {tok.value} is outside the allowed range"
940	            )

943	    def _expect_table_name(self) -> _Token:
944	        tok = self._peek()
945	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
946	            return self._next()
947	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected table name, got {tok.text!r}")

949	    def _parse_group_name(self) -> tuple:
950	        # Returns a (table|None, table_quoted, name) triple.
951	        tok = self._peek()
952	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
953	            raise QueryValidationError(
954	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not CASE expressions"
955	            )
956	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
957	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
958	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
959	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
960	            result = (item.table, item.table_quoted, item.name)
961	        else:
962	            self._next()
963	            result = (None, False, tok.value)
964	        # GROUP BY keeps accepting column references only; a scalar
965	        # expression in an aggregate query is a validation error.
966	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
967	            raise QueryValidationError(
968	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not expressions"
969	            )
970	        return result

972	    # HAVING expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
973	    #
974	    # HAVING shares the WHERE boolean structure (NOT / AND / OR / comparison /
975	    # IS [NOT] NULL, parentheses, typed literals) but its value operands are
976	    # restricted to grouping columns, aggregate calls and literals; CASE,
977	    # scalar arithmetic and nested aggregates are rejected.
978	
979	    def _parse_having_or(self) -> tuple:
980	        node = self._parse_having_and()
981	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
982	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_having_and())
983	        return node
984	
985	    def _parse_having_and(self) -> tuple:
986	        node = self._parse_having_comparison()
987	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
988	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_having_comparison())
989	        return node
990	
991	    def _parse_having_comparison(self) -> tuple:
992	        left = self._parse_having_not_factor()
993	        tok = self._peek()
994	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
995	            self._next()
996	            right = self._parse_having_not_factor()
997	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
998	        return left
999	
1000	    def _parse_having_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
1001	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
1002	            return ("not", self._parse_having_not_factor())
1003	        return self._parse_having_postfix()
1004	
1005	    def _parse_having_postfix(self) -> tuple:
1006	        node = self._parse_having_operand()
1007	        # HAVING operands stay scalar references; arithmetic on top of a
1008	        # group column or aggregate result is a validation error.
1009	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
1010	            raise QueryValidationError(
1011	                "HAVING does not allow scalar arithmetic expressions"
1012	            )
1013	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
1014	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
1015	            self._expect_keyword("null")
1016	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
1017	        return node
1018	
1019	    def _parse_having_operand(self) -> tuple:
1020	        tok = self._peek()
1021	        if self._accept_op("("):
1022	            node = self._parse_having_or()
1023	            self._expect_op(")")
1024	            return node
1025	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
1026	            # Only a signed numeric literal is accepted; unary +/- around a
1027	            # column or aggregate is scalar arithmetic and stays rejected.
1028	            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
1029	            if nxt.kind == "number" and not isinstance(nxt.value, bool):
1030	                self._next()
1031	                self._next()
1032	                value = nxt.value
1033	                if isinstance(value, int):
1034	                    if tok.value == "-":
1035	                        value = -value
1036	                    if not (_INT64_MIN <= value <= _INT64_MAX):
1037	                        raise QuerySyntaxError(
1038	                            "integer literal is outside the int64 range"
1039	                        )
1040	                    return ("literal", value, "int64")
1041	                return ("literal", -value if tok.value == "-" else value, "float64")
1042	            if nxt.kind == "eof":
1043	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
1044	                    f"expected a numeric literal after {tok.value!r} in HAVING"
1045	                )
1046	            raise QueryValidationError(
1047	                "HAVING does not allow scalar arithmetic expressions"
1048	            )
1049	        if tok.kind == "star":
1050	            raise QuerySyntaxError("'*' is not allowed in HAVING")
1051	        if tok.kind == "number":
1052	            self._next()
1053	            value = tok.value
1054	            if isinstance(value, bool):
1055	                return ("literal", value, "bool")
1056	            return (
1057	                "literal",
1058	                value,
1059	                "int64" if isinstance(value, int) else "float64",
1060	            )
1061	        if tok.kind == "string":
1062	            self._next()
1063	            return ("literal", tok.value, "utf8")
1064	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
1065	            if (
1066	                tok.kind == "ident"
1067	                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
1068	                and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
1069	                and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
1070	            ):
1071	                func = tok.value.lower()
1072	                self._next()  # function name
1073	                self._expect_op("(")
1074	                arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted, distinct = self._parse_aggregate_args(
1075	                    func
1076	                )
1077	                self._expect_op(")")
1078	                return (
1079	                    "hagg",
1080	                    func.upper(),
1081	                    arg,
1082	                    arg_table,
1083	                    arg_table_quoted,
1084	                    distinct,
1085	                )
1086	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
1087	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
1088	                return ("column", item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
1089	            if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
1090	                self._next()
1091	                return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
1092	            # An aggregate-style name not followed by '(' is a plain column.
1093	            self._next()
1094	            return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
1095	        if tok.kind == "keyword":
1096	            if tok.value == "case":
1097	                raise QueryValidationError("CASE expressions are not allowed in HAVING")
1098	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
1099	                f"unexpected keyword {tok.text.upper()!r} in HAVING expression"
1100	            )
1101	        raise QuerySyntaxError(
1102	            f"unexpected token {tok.text!r} in HAVING expression"
1103	        )

1105	    # WHERE expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
1106	
1107	    def _parse_or(self) -> tuple:
1108	        node = self._parse_and()
1109	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
1110	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_and())
1111	        return node
1112	
1113	    def _parse_and(self) -> tuple:
1114	        node = self._parse_comparison()
1115	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
1116	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_comparison())
1117	        return node

1119	    def _parse_comparison(self) -> tuple:
1120	        left = self._parse_not_factor()
1121	        tok = self._peek()
1122	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
1123	            self._next()
1124	            right = self._parse_not_factor()
1125	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
1126	        return left
1127	
1128	    def _parse_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
1129	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
1130	            return ("not", self._parse_not_factor())
1131	        return self._parse_postfix()

1133	    def _parse_postfix(self) -> tuple:
1134	        node = self._parse_arith()
1135	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
1136	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
1137	            self._expect_keyword("null")
1138	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
1139	        return node

1141	    # Arithmetic expressions (numeric scalar operands) ------------------------
1142	    # Precedence (highest first): parentheses, unary +/-, * /, + -.
1143	
1144	    def _parse_arith(self) -> tuple:
1145	        node = self._parse_term()
1146	        while True:
1147	            tok = self._peek()
1148	            if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
1149	                self._next()
1150	                node = ("arith", tok.value, node, self._parse_term())
1151	            else:
1152	                return node

1154	    def _parse_term(self) -> tuple:
1155	        node = self._parse_factor()
1156	        while True:
1157	            tok = self._peek()

1247	    def _parse_case(self) -> tuple:

1249	        # "ELSE result", terminated by END.  Conditions are boolean
1250	        # expressions; results are scalar (numeric, bool or utf8) and may
1251	        # themselves contain nested CASE expressions.  The simple form

1525	def _bind_aggregate(select: _Select, schema: Schema, where) -> dict:
1526	    if select.star:
1527	        raise QueryValidationError("'*' cannot be combined with aggregates or GROUP BY")

1529	    if (
1530	        select.having is not None
1531	        and select.group_by is None
1532	        and not select.has_aggregate
1533	        and not _having_tree_has_aggregate(select.having)
1534	    ):
1535	        # HAVING filters formed groups; without aggregation or GROUP BY the
1536	        # statement stays a non-aggregate query and HAVING has no meaning.
1537	        raise QueryValidationError(
1538	            "HAVING is only valid with GROUP BY or an aggregate"
1539	        )
1540	
1541	    # Resolve GROUP BY columns first: order matters for the grouping key, and
1542	    # duplicates / unknown columns are rejected here.  Entries are
1543	    # (table, table_quoted, name) triples; names reaching the binder are
1544	    # already canonical (single-file queries never carry a qualifier).
1545	    group_indices: list[int] = []

1547	    for _table, _table_quoted, name in select.group_by or ():
1548	        if name in group_seen:
1549	            raise QueryValidationError(f"duplicate column in GROUP BY: {name!r}")

1551	        try:
1552	            group_indices.append(schema.index(name))
1553	        except KeyError:
1554	            raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown GROUP BY column: {name!r}") from None
1555	    group_index_set = set(group_indices)
1556	
1557	    # One registry of distinct aggregates shared by SELECT, HAVING and ORDER
1558	    # BY, keyed by (function, argument index, DISTINCT flag) and kept in
1559	    # first-reference order.  HAVING-only aggregates are computed but never
1560	    # projected.

1564	    def require_aggregate(func: str, arg_name: str, distinct: bool = False) -> int:

1566	            func, arg_name, schema, distinct
1567	        )

1569	        slot = agg_registry.get(key)
1570	        if slot is None:
1571	            slot = len(agg_order)
1572	            agg_registry[key] = slot
1573	            agg_order.append(
1574	                _BoundItem(
1575	                    "agg",
1576	                    output_name=label,
1577	                    func=func,
1578	                    arg_index=arg_index,
1579	                    arg_type=arg_col.type if arg_col is not None else "",
1580	                    distinct=distinct,

1594	            raise QueryValidationError(
1595	                "'*' cannot be combined with aggregates or GROUP BY"
1596	            )

1600	            )

1606	            except KeyError:
1607	                raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
1608	            if col_index not in group_index_set:

1620	                    output_name=label,

1696	        except KeyError:

1717	        )

1720	        )
